report_name: K-Pop Agency HYBE Discloses Breach Exposing Employee, Partner Data

threat_actors.name: Unattributed
threat_actors.description: The unattributed threat actor responsible for the supply chain attack against HYBE Corporation, initiated by exploiting a vulnerability in a third-party document preview software. The actor exfiltrated sensitive PII of employees and partners and accessed the company's expense management system.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Attackers gained initial access by exploiting a vulnerability in a third-party document preview software used by HYBE, leveraging the trusted relationship between the company and its software vendor.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The attack originated from a compromise in a third-party software vendor, representing a supply chain attack to gain access to the target, HYBE Corporation.

attack_patterns.name: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: PowerShell was noted as a tool likely used for post-exploitation activities, such as discovery or lateral movement, within HYBE's network.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors collected a wide array of sensitive data from compromised systems, including identification numbers, medical records, passport details, and financial information.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: Collected sensitive data was exfiltrated from HYBE's network to attacker-controlled infrastructure, likely using web-based services to blend in with normal traffic.

tools.name: Unnamed third-party document preview software
tools.description: A vulnerable third-party document preview software integrated into HYBE's environment was the initial vector for the breach.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description: PowerShell was identified as a likely tool for executing commands for discovery and lateral movement post-compromise.

vulnerabilities.name: Vulnerability in third-party document preview software
vulnerabilities.description: An unknown vulnerability in a third-party document preview software integrated into HYBE's environment was exploited for initial access.

identities.name: HYBE Corporation
identities.description: The primary victim of the data breach. HYBE is a South Korean entertainment company that manages K-pop group BTS.

identities.name: BTS
identities.description: High-profile K-pop group managed by HYBE, mentioned for context.

identities.name: HYBE Employees and Business Partners
identities.description: A class of individuals whose sensitive personal information, including medical records and financial data, was exposed in the breach.

infrastructure.name: Attacker-controlled Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: The infrastructure used by the attackers to receive the exfiltrated data from HYBE's network.

indicators.name: PowerShell Process Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution
id: 2b8a1c9d-5e6f-4a3b-8c1d-9e8f7a6b5c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of powershell.exe, which could indicate post-exploitation activity as mentioned in the HYBE breach analysis.
references:
  - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8VIT2ZRF4w
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Anomalous Outbound Traffic from Third-Party Application Servers
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Outbound Traffic from Third-Party Application Servers
id: 8c1d9e8f-7a6b-4c5d-a3b2-1c9d8e7f6a5b
status: experimental
description: Detects potentially large or unusual outbound data transfers from servers hosting third-party applications, which could indicate data exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8VIT2ZRF4w
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
tags:
  - attack.t1567
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    # This is a conceptual rule. Specific source IPs of third-party servers should be added.
    sc-bytes|gt: 10000000 # Example threshold for large transfer (10MB)
  condition: selection

indicators.name: PowerShell Filename Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: PowerShell File Event
id: 3d9e8f7a-6b5c-4d8e-b2a1-c9d8e7f6a5b4
status: experimental
description: Detects file events involving powershell.exe, which could be part of staging post-exploitation tools.
references:
  - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8VIT2ZRF4w
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
level: low
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
  condition: selection
